title: KVCache eviction throughput probe notes
content:
Goal: collect a compact, reproducible set of observations and commands for the suspected KV-cache eviction-driven throughput regression. This is a working scratchpad — hypothesis-driven, with exact commands to re-run on staging clusters.

Background / short summary:
- Over the last 2 weeks we've observed reduced tokens/sec on some p99 workloads after a rollout to change continuous-batch warmup and batch_window_ms defaults (see INF-5023).
- Most affected: mid-length chat workloads (seq_len 512–1024) with frequent short-turn requests that rely heavily on KV-cache hits for cost/latency.
- Suspect: accidental interactions between continuous-batching warmup, aggressive KV-cache cleanup, and async handoff causing transient cache thrash + extra KV cache population work per request.

What I saw (staging snapshot 2024-09-16):
- Baseline throughput (before change): ~1250 tok/s per GPU for sample workload (steady-state).
- After change: dropped to ~820 tok/s (approx -35%).
- Latency tail increased: p50 unchanged, p95 ~ +120 ms, p99 ~ +490 ms.
- Runtime logs show spikes in `kv_cache_evictions` and `kv_cache_populate_latency_ms` around the same time as throughput drops.

Key log snippets (redacted trace ids):
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] INFO serving.runtime.batch: batch_handled id=abc123 size=6 latency_ms=22
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] DEBUG serving.runtime.kvcache: key=chat-ctx-.. hit=true 
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] INFO serving.runtime.kvcache: kv_cache_eviction_count=312 policy=LRU threshold=0.65
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] WARN serving.runtime.kvcache: populate_latency_ms=84 reason=full-fill
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] INFO serving.runtime.batch: handoff async-start id=abc124
[2024-09-16T14:21:03Z] DEBUG serving.runtime.kvcache: key=chat-ctx-.. hit=false // subsequent repopulation

Error / unexpected behavior observed:
- `kv_cache_eviction_count` jumps in short bursts right after continuous-batch warmup completes for a warmup interval. Evictions correlate with higher `populate_latency_ms` and immediate cache misses.
- Batch handoff path appears to spawn async population tasks that race with normal request serving, leading to duplicated populate work and thrash.
- Memory usage on GPU hosts briefly dips and then spikes — consistent with eviction+repopulation cycles.

Commands I ran (staging; run as svc-debug or eng account):
1) Reproduce traffic: replay recorded trace (trace-id: replay-20240915-10) against staging gateway: 
   loadgen --profile chat-midseq --replay replay-20240915-10 --concurrency 50 --rps 1200 --target staging 
2) Tail logs with filters: 
   rg "kv_cache|populate_latency|eviction" /var/log/serving-runtime/*.log -n | sed -n '1,200p'
3) Counter snapshots from /debug/metrics (host): 
   curl -s http://localhost:8888/debug/metrics | rg kv_cache | sort
4) Live perf and stacks while repro running: 
   sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 30; sudo perf script -i /tmp/perf.data | head -n 200
   sudo jstack $(pidof serving-runtime) > /tmp/jstack.txt
5) Check BPF tracepoints to see async worker scheduling around handoff: 
   sudo bpftool prog -j | rg handoff; sudo ./scripts/bpf/trace-handoff.o --duration 30

Quick measurements (staging run 2024-09-16):
- baseline run (old config): tok/s=1248, p99=380ms, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.92
- after-change run: tok/s=820, p99=870ms, kv_cache_hit_rate=0.71
- peak eviction bursts: 300–600 evictions over 10s windows (metric: kv_cache_eviction_count.delta)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between warmup population and request-time population: warmup triggers async populate tasks that prefill keys but configure them with lower refcounts / different lifetime metadata; when real requests hit, the runtime treats warmup entries as stale and repopulates, causing double work + eviction pressure.
2) Eviction policy/threshold misconfigured: recent change lowered capacity threshold to 0.65 (from 0.8), so normal churn is now evicting useful keys aggressively. Continuous-batch warmup amplifies churn because it creates many short-lived keys.
3) Handoff async worker backlog: if handoff queue is full, async populates get retried and cause extra allocations that trigger eviction.
4) Slab allocator fragmentation: warmup/populate patterns create fragmentation that reduces effective capacity; eviction counts go up even though raw allocated memory looks ok.

Evidence supporting 1 & 2:
- Logs show `policy=LRU threshold=0.65` (recent config change).
- Warmup interval traces show prefill events immediately before large evictions.
- Re-running with threshold bumped back to 0.85 reduces eviction bursts and recovers ~90% of throughput in quick experiments.

Quick experiments I ran / notes:
- Toggle `kv_cache.capacity_threshold` from 0.65 -> 0.85 on a single node, restart runtime: tok/s moved from 820 -> 1110 (partial recovery).
- Disable continuous-batch warmup on a canary node: throughput recovered to ~1180 tok/s (baseline-ish) but increased cold-start p50 slightly.
- Instrumented populate path to increment `populate_origin` tag = {warmup|request|handoff} and saw ~45% of populates during regression marked as `warmup` and ~40% `handoff` (duplicates for same key within 2s window).

Reproducer steps (minimal):
1) Start a single-worker staging node with changed config:
   export KV_CACHE_THRESHOLD=0.65
   export CONT_BATCH_WARMUP=enabled
   ./deploy_dev node --single-worker --debug-kvcache
2) Run loadgen profile above.
3) Tail metrics as described and verify eviction burst pattern.

Data to collect from prod-like cluster if we want to confirm:
- kv_cache_eviction_count (delta per 10s) per host
- kv_cache_hit_rate per route/model (tagged)
- populate_origin counts and a sampling of keys that got repopulated within 5s window
- handoff queue length / retries
- gpu-memory fragmentation/fallback stats
- perf stacks sampled during eviction spikes

Immediate mitigations to try (low-risk ordered):
1) Raise kv_cache.capacity_threshold to 0.8–0.9 in canary (quick config change).
2) Rate-limit warmup population: only prefill N keys per second per worker for active routes.
3) Make warmup populate mark entries with a slightly longer TTL or higher refcount to avoid being immediately evicted.
4) Add dedupe in populate path: if key already in-flight population, do not spawn duplicate task.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Rethink eviction policy or introduce a short-term immunity window for newly-populated keys from warmup.
- Tweak slab allocator to avoid fragmentation from repeated small allocations pattern.
- Improve instrumentation: add per-key lifecycle tracing (cheap sampling) to measure warmup vs request population overlap.

Open questions / TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Samir to try 0.85 threshold canary across 3 nodes and report perf2 numbers (assigned INF-5023).
- [ ] Lena to produce a heatmap of populate_origin for top-100 keys across 24h window (query from metrics store).
- [ ] I (Maya) to add a quick dedupe flag to populate worker and test whether duplicates reduce eviction. Patch draft at: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2512
- [ ] Decide whether to delay rollout of warmup defaults until dedupe/immunity implemented.

Notes to self: keep this doc as a running timeline. If we confirm threshold is the main lever we can add a short-term runtime config that auto-scales threshold based on current eviction delta to avoid ramp regressions during rollouts.

Appendix: useful commands / queries
- metrics query (prometheus-ish):
  sum by (instance) (increase(kv_cache_eviction_count[1m]))
  sum by (route) (rate(kv_cache_populate_total[5m]))
  sum by (populate_origin) (increase(kv_cache_populate_total[1m]))
- sample keys that were repopulated within window (requires debug endpoint):
  curl localhost:9001/debug/kvcache/sample?since=5s | jq .repop_hits | head -n 50

End of notes (2024-10-02). Will update after Samir's canary and the dedupe test.
